Any settlement more than one week past the last row returns last_period_before_settlement: it states how many weeks are bridged and is not a fault, but it is the horizon the forecast rests on. history_stale applies when the latest row is more than 7 days old.

HOUSING. Starts: HOUST. Permits: PERMIT. Case-Shiller national: CSUSHPISA. All monthly, seasonally adjusted; HOUST and PERMIT are annual rates in thousands, resolved from 'housing starts' and 'building permits' in the text, CSUSHPISA from 'case-shiller'. 'Home sales' and 'home prices' without Case-Shiller are not resolved: pass series and table, or series_sql with frequency. HOUST and PERMIT default to level; CSUSHPISA has no default, pass transform (level, mom_pct or yoy_pct). Where the rules state no units, a thousands series flags units_mismatch: the strikes may be in single units, and the forecast is unverified against them. With as_of, a row counts as known 21 days after month end for starts and permits, 62 for Case-Shiller.

You MUST state every flag. A settlement period the catalog already holds is an error: query the value. For a Kalshi edge call backtest_market_forecast(source='kalshi', series=<venue series>) when confidence.backtest is null; Polymarket has no backtest.

recipes.title: Weather events on Kalshi or Polymarket (temperature, precipitation, storms): the forecast builder does not resolve them, so the forecast is a climatology from samples_sql
recipes.body:
Drivers temperature (title matches temperature, hottest, coldest or a degree sign) and precipitation (rain, rainfall, snow, snowfall, precipitation) have basis climatology and tables weather.ghcnd_daily and weather.climate_normals_monthly. A temperature or precipitation event is listed only when its title names a United States place the screen knows (a list of large cities, 'us', 'u.s.', 'united states'); a title naming only a state, or any other place, is not listed. A storms event has no place test. storms (how many hurricanes, tornadoes, named storms; disasters.storm_events) is also climatology.

The forecast builder has no resolver for these drivers: price_market_event(build_forecast=true) and forecast_market_event fail, and scan_market_opportunities lists the event under not_forecast. Build the forecast from rows:
1) price_market_event(source, event_id) with no forecast: read the rules for the station or place, the measured quantity, the units, the window and the rounding.
2) describe_table on weather.ghcnd_daily (or the normals table), then write samples_sql: the same station and the same calendar window in every past year, one row per year, the first column the settlement value in the strikes' units, no NULLs, under 5000 rows. A storm count is the count in the same window of each past year.
3) price_market_event(source, event_id, samples_sql=..., round=...) for the event on each venue. Polymarket markets carry no structured strike: pass conditions for each market_id in the sample's units.

WHAT IT IS. The distribution is every past year's value for that window: it knows nothing of the current season or any weather forecast, so it is least reliable close to settlement, when the market has forecasts the sample lacks. Check data_coverage: a table that stops before the window, or a station with missing years, thins the sample. A forecast you pass in has no engine backtest: confidence is weak with the reason 'the forecast was given by the caller', to be stated with the edge. Where the venue settles on a station the warehouse does not carry, say so and do not substitute another station without saying it.

recipes.title: Oil-price and Treasury-yield events (touch, stay above, close at): forecast_market_event replays historical paths, and window_start sets the bound already reached
triggers: oil price at any time event
how high will oil go market
recipes.body:
Drivers energy_price (title matches crude, wti, brent, gas prices, gasoline, natural gas; basis market_price) and treasury_yield (treasury yield, treasury spread, yield curve) are resolved in part. Build with price_market_event(source, event_id, build_forecast=true) or forecast_market_event(source, event_id), for the event on each venue.

OIL. WTI crude is DCOILWTICO, daily, dollars per barrel, proportional changes (econ.fred_indicators), resolved when the text says wti or crude. A text that says brent, or a rules text naming DCOILBRENTEU, returns series_not_sourced and no forecast: you MUST NOT price it against WTI. Gas prices, gasoline and natural gas are not resolved: the call fails and asks for series and table. Default history is 5 years of daily rows.

TRANSFORM. max_path when the text says 'at any time', 'at any point', 'touch', 'how high', 'highest' or 'maximum' with during, between, through or before, or 'above ... on any day'; min_path for 'how low', 'below ... on any day', or 'lowest' or 'minimum' with during, between, through or before; level otherwise (the series default). A text that matches more than one transform is an error: pass transform.

METHOD. h is the number of trading days from the last row to the settlement date, round(calendar days x 5 / 7); the settlement date is the event's close date unless settlement_period is given. For a path transform each historical h-day path is replayed from the latest price by its proportional moves, and the sample is that path's highest (max_path) or lowest (min_path) value. Pass window_start, the ISO date the event's window began: the highest (lowest) value the series has already reached since then floors (caps) every sample, since a barrier already touched cannot be un-touched. Omitting it on a window already open understates the probability of a touch.

FLAGS. You MUST state every flag. For a path transform last_period_before_settlement is returned when the last row is more than 5 days before today; history_stale applies past 5 days for a daily series. The distribution is of past price paths, a band and not a direction; the model of the volatility behind it can be checked with backtest_volatility on the price series.

TREASURY YIELDS. The tenor is read from the text ('10-year', '3-month') and must be exactly one: DGS3MO, DGS2, DGS5, DGS10 and DGS30 are in the catalog; another tenor returns series_not_sourced, and none or several is an error asking for series. The series is daily, in percent, additive, level by default.

recipes.title: Cross-venue basket: the same event on Polymarket and Kalshi, what makes the floor real, and why both venues are always priced
triggers: same event on kalshi and polymarket
locked yield across kalshi and polymarket
recipes.body:
A cross_venue basket (find_market_baskets recipe cross_venue) holds events of one driver on both venues, chained by close date: each closes no more than 3 days after the one before it. It needs no forecast: it is a test of whether the two sets of quotes leave a gap whatever the settlement value turns out to be. Both venues are always in it; price_market_basket on events from one venue returns a venue_note saying to check the other.

TEST. price_market_basket(events=[the Kalshi event, the Polymarket event], lock=true, scenario_grid=true, search=2..4, min_yield as asked). Give both events the same column (the quantity they settle on). A Polymarket market has no structured strike: state a condition for every Polymarket market_id in conditions, in that column's units ({"<market_id>": {"above": 3.0}}). scenario_grid scores every distinct outcome of the column: each strike and a value in every gap between, below and above them. Each leg is bought at the quote on both sides of every market; the basket is kept only when its worst case, the lowest payout over all outcomes less cost, is positive after fees. The floor is that worst case over cost. When the search keeps a basket and its events share one column, the result carries payoff_curve (profit per cost by settlement value, fee-inclusive floor and break-evens).

WHAT MAKES THE FLOOR REAL. 1) Rules. Two events are one outcome only if their rules agree on source, period, rounding and the other dimensions. compare_settlement_rules(a={source, event_id}, b={source, event_id}) diffs nine: source_agency, series, settlement_period, transform, seasonal_adjustment, rounding, release_or_close_date, revision_handling, tie_handling. rules_match is match only when every dimension is stated on both sides and agrees, differ when any differs, unverified when none differs but some are not stated; an unstated dimension is never counted as equal. You MUST call it for every cross-venue pair before calling a basket a lock. You MUST report a lock whose rules_match is not match as not a lock, naming each differing and unknown dimension. price_market_basket and find_market_baskets return rules_match on the pairs they hold. 2) Fees. Every leg pays a taker fee at its quote: Kalshi 0.07 x the series' fee_multiplier x p x (1 - p), Polymarket the market's fee schedule rate (zero where fees are off). The fee is largest near 50 cents and is paid on both legs, so a gross gap of a few points is often gone: report the gross gap and the floor net of fees. 3) Depth and capital are not modelled in the basket: read the top of each leg's book (best bid and ask with their sizes) with market_price_history. A ticket with depth comes only from price_market_event with a forecast, for a market it finds mispriced. The basket's yield is to settlement, not annualized.

REPORT. Legs with venue and side, cost, fees, floor, payoff_curve, rules_match with its differing and unknown dimensions, scenario basis and row count. 'No lock after fees' is a finding: say it, with the closest case.

recipes.title: same_place basket: different quantities settling on one state or city, and how to price them as one position
triggers: weather and crop events same state
recipes.body:
A same_place basket (find_market_baskets recipe same_place) holds events of at least two different drivers whose titles name the same state; a named city counts as its state (for example nyc as new york, houston as texas). Its why, 'different quantities measured in one state', is a hypothesis that one local shock moves them together, not a measurement. Events from both venues are eligible; check that the basket holds both, or say which venue had none.

PRICE IT. 1) Measure the link: fetch_aligned_series on each event's settlement series for that state, then correlation_matrix. A basket whose series do not co-move is a set of independent bets, not a hedge. 2) Forecast each event (price_market_event with build_forecast=true where the driver resolves, else the forecast routes in the per-driver recipes), giving each event its own column. 3) price_market_basket(events=[...], scenarios_sql=<one row per historical period with a numeric column per event column, no NULLs, under 5000 rows>). Scenarios drawn from the aligned history keep the correlation between events; independent inline scenarios do not. Without lock the legs are each event's mispriced markets, so every event needs a forecast; state every Polymarket market's condition in its column's units. 4) With scenario probabilities the result carries p_profit, p_loss, expected and yield; yield is to settlement, not annualized. search=k scores every subset of up to k legs.

REPORT per leg: venue, side, price, fee, edge; for the basket cost, floor, best case, p_profit, the scenario basis and row count, and what would break the link (a local shock hitting one quantity and not another).

recipes.title: linked_drivers basket: events whose drivers are joined by a causal chain, the five chains the finder knows, and what the direction does and does not say
triggers: weather crop yield commodity prices basket
recipes.body:
A linked_drivers basket (find_market_baskets recipe linked_drivers, match=<link name>) holds events of two or more drivers that sit on one chain. The chains, with drivers in causal order, cause first: agriculture (temperature, precipitation, drought, crop_yield, livestock, tariffs, food_prices, inflation); prices_and_policy (energy_price, food_prices, tariffs, inflation, pce, policy_rate, treasury_yield, mortgage_rate); labor_and_growth (payrolls, unemployment, jobless_claims, output, policy_rate); rates_and_housing (policy_rate, treasury_yield, mortgage_rate, housing); energy_and_weather (temperature, storms, gas_storage, energy_price, inflation). link_direction lists the drivers present in that order. The order is the causal chain; the sign of each link is not asserted, so measure it.

Finder defaults keep bases release, climatology and policy; pass basis with market_price added or energy_price and treasury_yield events are not in the basket. Both venues' events are included; say which venue each leg is on.

PRICE IT. 1) fetch_aligned_series on the settlement series of each driver present, then correlation_matrix: the measured sign and size of each link, and whether it holds in the window the events settle in. 2) Forecast each event; the forecast routes differ by driver (see the per-driver forecasting recipes). 3) price_market_basket with scenarios_sql over the aligned history (one numeric column per event column) so the correlation is kept, or scenarios from scenario_sweep rows. 4) Read p_profit, expected, yield (to settlement) and the scenario row count. A link that is lagged (cause leads effect by a period) needs the aligned query to shift the cause by that lag.

A basket's why is a hypothesis. You MUST NOT report a basket as an arbitrage before price_market_basket has scored it net of fees. A basket of correlated bets is a position with a probability of profit, not a lock, unless lock=true finds a positive floor.

recipes.title: series_run basket: one venue series over consecutive periods, and how to price a surprise carrying from one period into the next
recipes.body:
A series_run basket (find_market_baskets recipe series_run) holds two or more events with the same venue series ticker on one venue, for example the monthly events of one Kalshi series. Its why, 'one series over consecutive periods', is a hypothesis that a surprise in one period carries into the next. It stays on one venue by construction, so check the other venue for the same release (find_market_baskets recipe cross_venue) and price it too.

PRICE IT. 1) Measure the persistence in the settlement series itself: query its history (fetch_aligned_series with the series against its own lag, or a lagged self-join in a query) and correlate the transform the events settle on, not the level. 2) Forecast each event with build_forecast=true. The forecasts of later periods rest on the same last row, so their errors are not independent: use a joint basis. 3) Give each event its own column (each settles on a different period) and give price_market_basket scenarios_sql with one row per historical run of consecutive periods, a numeric column per event column, no NULLs. 4) Read p_profit, expected and yield (to settlement); with lock=true only a positive-floor subset is a lock.

Where the earlier period has already settled, its event is gone from the open listing: the later ones price off a known value once the catalog holds that period: last_period moves forward when the release is ingested, not when the venue settles. An earlier period's printed value is a reason to re-price, with a new build_forecast, not a number to carry by hand.

recipes.title: range basket: YES on one event's lowest strike and NO on its highest, a collar that pays most inside the strikes and is a lock only on an inverted ladder
triggers: lowest strike yes highest strike no
recipes.body:
A range basket (find_market_baskets recipe range) is built inside one event's ladder of above or at-least strikes: buy YES on the lowest strike and NO on the highest. With strict above strikes the pair pays 2 when the settlement lands between the strikes and 1 outside them, so it always pays at least 1 and pays most inside the range. It is one event on one venue.

WHEN IT IS A LOCK. The pair costs the lower strike's YES ask plus one less the higher strike's YES bid, plus a taker fee on each leg. It costs less than 1 only if the lower strike's YES is offered for less than the higher strike's YES is bid, an inverted ladder. Buying YES on the lower strike and selling YES on the higher then cannot lose; whether it still locks after fees is the question. On any other ladder the pair costs more than 1 before fees for a payout of at least 1: not a lock, a bet that the settlement lands in the range.

PRICE IT. price_market_event on the event returns structural_locks net of fees (ladder pairs that still lock, and the event's bucket partition), with no forecast. To score the pair: price_market_basket(events=[that event], lock=true, scenario_grid=true, search=2). The Kalshi strikes are structured; Polymarket markets need conditions stated per market_id. When the search keeps a pair, the result carries payoff_curve with the fee-inclusive floor; a pair that does not lock is not kept and no payoff_curve is returned. Without lock a one-event basket holds only the legs a forecast finds mispriced, not the range pair: no call scores the pair as a bet.

Fees are 0.07 x fee_multiplier x p x (1 - p) per contract on Kalshi, the market's schedule on Polymarket, and are largest near 50 cents: a ladder gap of one or two points rarely survives two fees. Report the gross gap and the net floor. Depth behind the two quotes is not modelled: read the top of both books (best bid and ask with their sizes) with market_price_history before calling it capturable. Check the other venue for an event on the same quantity: both are always in scope.

recipes.title: calendar basket: one driver on one venue at two adjacent close dates, priced as a spread between periods
recipes.body:
A calendar basket (find_market_baskets recipe calendar) holds the events of one driver on one venue at exactly two adjacent close dates, whatever their series tickers, so the spread between the two periods can be priced as a pair. series_run instead holds every period of one series ticker. A driver quoted on both venues gives a calendar basket on each; they are separate baskets.

PRICE IT. 1) The two events settle on different periods, so give them different columns. 2) Forecast each with build_forecast=true (or the per-driver route); the later period's forecast bridges more periods from the same last row, so its flags (last_period_before_settlement) differ and each is stated. 3) The legs share a driver, so their outcomes are not independent: price_market_basket with scenarios_sql, one row per historical pair of the two periods of the settlement series' transform (a numeric column per event column, no NULLs), keeps that dependence. Independent inline scenarios do not. 4) Read p_profit, expected, yield (to settlement); with lock=true only a positive-floor subset is a lock, and two different periods rarely give one.

The two close dates may fall on either side of a release: once the catalog holds a new period of the settlement series (a period after last_period), a ticket from a built forecast re-quotes as void, for both events alike, so re-price after a release. State each leg's venue, side, price, fee and edge, and the scenario basis and row count.

recipes.title: Acting on a mispricing: quotes are a point in time, the ticket carries a limit and void conditions, and requote_market_opportunity says whether it is still there
triggers: can i still take this mispricing
recipes.body:
No tool trades for the user. Every price in a result is a quote read at one moment: quotes_read_at on every priced event and scan row, quote_time on an event priced against a forecast and on each ticket. An opportunity reported minutes ago may be gone.

TICKET. Each mispriced market from price_market_event carries a ticket: source, event_id, market_id, side, limit_price (the highest price on the 0.01 tick at which edge is still at least min_edge after the fee), fair, fee_rate, min_edge, edge_at_limit, quote_time, size when size was passed, and void_conditions. When no price on the side clears min_edge on the tick, ticket is null with a ticket_note: report that there is no ticket at that min_edge. The row also carries days_to_settlement, annualized_return_simple_365d (return on cost x 365 / days, simple, omitted under one day), and breakeven_fair, the fair value at which the edge is zero. Depth is read for the 3 largest edges only: contracts_at_or_under_limit and dollars_at_or_under_limit; pass size and the row adds the fill's average price, fee and edge walking the book (fill_edge), and whether the size fills completely under the limit. A market whose depth was not read says so: its quote is top of book and its depth is unknown.

VOID CONDITIONS. settlement_close: the market's close time. settlement_series_release: present when the engine built the forecast; the ticket is void once the catalog holds a period of the settlement series after the last_period the forecast started from, because the forecast is then one release behind.

RE-QUOTE. Asked whether an opportunity is still there, you MUST call requote_market_opportunity(ticket) with the ticket object exactly as returned. status open: the ticket's size (at least one contract when it has none) rests at or under limit_price. partly_open: only contracts_left rest at or under it; contracts_left is what rests at or under the limit, not the unfilled part of the ticket. gone: nothing rests at or under limit_price (give current_best_price and edge_at_current_best), or the market closed (book_status closed, no price returned). void: a void condition occurred (voided_by); you MUST NOT report it as available. Always state requoted_at. A re-quote reads the book again and does not recompute the fair value: edge_at_current_best uses the ticket's fair. For a new fair value after a release, price the event again with price_market_event(build_forecast=true), which returns a new ticket.

REPORT per opportunity: venue, market, side, limit_price, depth, size and its fill edge if given, void_conditions, quote_time, annualized_return_simple_365d, breakeven_fair, and the re-quote status with requoted_at when it was asked. Both Polymarket and Kalshi are in scope: a market priced on one venue is checked against the other venue's counterpart.
